contract.title: ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present
contract.intent: Request a compact, editable ERA5 single-level reanalysis slice for surface meteorology fields over a bounded region and time period.
contract.summary: ERA5 is ECMWF/Copernicus global hourly gridded reanalysis from 1940 to present on single levels, including atmospheric, land-surface, and ocean-wave quantities. This draft selects a small default CONUS January 2024 hourly subset with common near-surface weather variables.
access_methods: Climate Data Store web download form
Climate Data Store API using cdsapi
credential_requirements: CDS personal access token stored under credential name CDS_API_TOKEN
Manual acceptance of the dataset Terms of Use in the CDS portal before download

fields.name: 10m_u_component_of_wind
fields.description: Eastward component of wind at 10 metres.

fields.name: 10m_v_component_of_wind
fields.description: Northward component of wind at 10 metres.

defaults_used: No user goal was provided, so selected common near-surface weather fields.
Limited date range to one complete historical month to keep the initial request small.
Limited geography to an approximate CONUS bounding box for a manageable regional subset.
Used product_type=reanalysis rather than ensemble products for a simple deterministic baseline.
Requested all hourly UTC timesteps because the dataset is hourly and diurnal information is often useful.
assumptions: The intended use is exploratory weather/climate extraction rather than ensemble uncertainty analysis.
Single-level data are appropriate; no pressure-level or model-level variables are requested.
The user can refine the region, variables, and time range before running a full extraction.
risks_or_unknowns: Expanding to multiple years, global coverage, or many variables can create very large downloads.
Recent ERA5T data are updated with about 5-day latency and can differ from the final ERA5 release until overwritten roughly 2 to 3 months later.
Accumulated variables such as total_precipitation require care when aggregating or interpreting hourly values.
The dataset page lists a CC-BY licence; attribution requirements should be preserved in downstream use.
Some known ERA5 data issues affect specific variables, dates, or regions; review the ERA5 documentation if using this for publication or high-stakes analysis.
